must_include.fact: Granting a model of a virtual-model account to another subject needs the provider-account-manager role on that parent account (or tenant admin); with it the same grant returns 201
Use access alone is not enough: provider-integration-access on the model, or provider-account-access (User) on the parent account, still returns 403 naming the parent account id

must_not.fact: Says the user needs to be made tenant admin as the only fix
Says use access (provider-account-access / User role on the parent) is enough
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: An account-level grant (provider-account-access on the parent account) makes /models list every model of that account regardless of the narrower per-model grant
Revoking only the account-level grant (DELETE /api/svc/v2/authorization with the same grant body) returns the list to just the per-model grants
The extra models are only that provider account's models, not the whole tenant; the list can also hold models the account sees through other grants

must_not.fact: Says it is an authorization leak or security bug
Says the list contains every model in the tenant

must_include.fact: The manifest permissions still reference a provider-integration FQN of a model that has since been removed from its provider account; the same manifest returned 200 before the removal
Fix: remove the stale permission entry for the deleted model and re-apply, which returns 200
Validation runs over every permission FQN in the full submitted manifest, so an unchanged re-apply or a tag-only update of the stored manifest fails the same way

must_not.fact: Says the error is transient or tells the user to retry
Calls it a platform bug

must_include.fact: In the tested shapes (virtual-account and agent bearers, the agent not set up as a delegating collaborator), only the Authorization bearer is authorised on the LLM gateway; x-tfy-agent-authorization changed no outcome

To be allowed, the bearer itself must be the identity holding the grant: an agent token sent as Authorization returns 200, an ungranted agent token returns 403 even with a granted agent's token in the header

must_not.fact: Says x-tfy-agent-authorization is enforced or restricts the call on the LLM gateway
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: A virtual account with ownedBy.team does not receive the team's grants; with a team-only role-binding its token lists no servers
Fix: add the virtual account as a second subject of the same role-binding (subjects team + virtualaccount), then the account's token lists the server
The role is mcp-server-user on the mcp-server resource, declared once in that binding for both subjects

must_not.fact: Says the team ownership should have granted access and it is a bug
Says the virtual account must be made a member of the team

must_include.fact: Figma has no entry in the tenant's official remote MCP catalogue: the catalogue-proxy mcp-integrations index (225 entries) contains no Figma at all

must_not.fact: Tells the user to try other spellings or clear caches/filters to make Figma appear
States that Figma is in the official catalogue and should be found
Tells the user to upgrade their plan to get Figma

must_include.fact: The 500 is raised by the gateway itself (error_origin_level gateway) because it could not get a token from the configured token endpoint; the call is not sent upstream
The auth/status reason field carries the token endpoint's HTTP status (e.g. 'Token endpoint request failed with status 400'); authentication_not_required there does not mean no auth is needed
The caller receives the gateway's own HTTP 500 (error_origin_level gateway), not an upstream 401 or a forwarded result

must_not.fact: Says the gateway forwards the call without a bearer and the upstream's own 401 reaches the caller
Says authentication_not_required means the server needs no auth

must_include.fact: The list endpoints return only the MCP servers the caller holds a role on; admin sees all, a virtual account sees just the servers it was granted
Fix: a role-binding with subject virtualaccount, role mcp-server-user, resourceType mcp-server and resourceFqn truefoundry:mcp-server:<name>
Listing does not change the auth record: the OAuth server's auth/status stays authentication_required ('No OAuth2 auth record found') before and after

must_not.fact: Says listing creates an auth record for the user
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: Re-applying the MCP server manifest with collaborators: [] returns 200 and clears the collaborator grants (e.g. agent:<name>); the agent then gets 403
Grants made as a role-binding (e.g. a virtual account with mcp-server-user) survive collaborators: [], so role-binding is the durable way to grant

must_not.fact: Says the agent token expired and must be regenerated
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: A per-virtual-account budget rule cannot have users or teams in when.subjects (in or not_in); the 400 ends 'includes users' or 'includes teams'
Fix: remove users/teams from when.subjects and keep only virtual_accounts; adding another virtual account then saves with 200
applies_to cannot be changed after the budget is created (403), so a different applies_to type needs a new rule

must_not.fact: Tells the user to change applies_to of the existing rule to per-user
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: The budget-exceeded response carries the header x-should-retry: false, on both /chat/completions and the Anthropic-shaped /v1/messages
No Retry-After header is sent on that response
The response is HTTP 429 and names the rule: x-tfy-applied-rules shows budget_limiting with violated true

must_not.fact: Says the gateway gives the client no signal to stop retrying
Calls it a gateway bug

must_include.fact: A per-user rule does not match requests authenticated with a virtual account token; x-tfy-applied-rules never names it for those calls (it blocks user identities, e.g. a PAT, with 429)
Fix: use a per-virtual-account rule with the same filters; then the VA's calls get 429 naming that rule

must_not.fact: Says a per-user rule applies to virtual account traffic and the budget just needs time or a lower limit
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: PUT /api/svc/v1/llm-gateway/installations rejects a manifest without isDefault with 422, on create and on an update that only sets enabled false

Workaround: PUT the full manifest with enabled: false and isDefault set (false for a non-default installation, otherwise keep the current value); it returns 200 and the installation shows enabled false

must_not.fact: Says the failure is transient or an outage
Tells the user to delete and recreate the installation

must_include.fact: By default a provider 400 is returned to the caller; adding "400" to the target's fallback_status_codes makes it fail over and the second target serves it (200)
fallback_status_codes replaces the default list rather than extending it: with ["400"] a 401 on target 1 is returned, so keep the other codes you still want to fail over on
400s that failed over did not demote target 1: later normal requests were still served by it

must_not.fact: Says 400 already fails over by default
Says an empty list makes everything fail over

must_include.fact: Either the request header x-tfy-openai-use-responses-api: true or output_config {effort: low} in the /v1/messages body makes the tool call return 200 with a tool_use block
The 400 is the provider's own validation passed through (api_error), not a gateway rule

must_not.fact: Says reasoning_effort none or enabling thinking in the /v1/messages body fixes it
Calls it a gateway bug

must_include.fact: Those 400s are Anthropic's own validation passed through: the Haiku target rejects adaptive thinking and effort while the same fields to a Sonnet target return 200

Setting override_params {thinking: null, output_config: null} on the Haiku target strips the fields and both requests return 200 (the docs' alternative, naming or splitting the virtual model so Claude Code sends Haiku-compatible requests, also counts)
A temperature-only override still returns 400 (now a temperature error); only the explicit null removes thinking/output_config

must_not.fact: Says override_params cannot remove client-chosen fields
Calls it a gateway bug

must_include.fact: The skip is how dry-run treats a virtual account whose permissions depend on a manifest in the same directory (tested: provider-account-access on a provider account whose manifest is in the dir); an integration-only virtual account in the same run is validated
When the provider account is already live and its manifest is not in the directory, the same virtual account is validated in dry-run
tfy apply --help (CLI 0.17.4) has no flag to force validation of skipped manifests

must_not.fact: Suggests a --force or --validate flag
Says skipped manifests were validated

must_include.fact: Those UI headers and the body user field are not used for metrics grouping: requests carrying them left no per-person row (the email appears nowhere in grouped metrics)
Fix: send the person in an X-TFY-METADATA header (JSON such as {"owui_user": "bob"}); it appears in metrics/query grouped by metadata.owui_user with count and cost per value
An enforce-mode budget keyed on that metadata key (applies_to type metadata) returns 429 to that person while another person on the same virtual account still gets 200

must_not.fact: Says the X-OpenWebUI-User headers or the user field are picked up automatically for attribution
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: A virtual account token with no tenant role gets 200 with zero dataPoints rather than a 403
The query is valid (the admin key returns rows); the caller only sees rows it is allowed to see, so use an admin key or grant the account access to the data

must_not.fact: Says the query, groupBy or body is wrong, or that the account has no traffic
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket

must_include.fact: The model reasons by default; the gateway keeps a plain Chat Completions request on /chat/completions unless it asks for reasoning (effort other than none, or a thinking field) or carries the opt-in header, and the provider's validation 400 is passed through
Fix: send the header x-tfy-openai-use-responses-api: true; the request is then served via the Responses API and returns 200 with a resp_ id
Alternatively set reasoning_effort to low/medium/high (or a thinking field), served via Responses (200); reasoning_effort none also returns 200 but stays on plain Chat Completions

must_not.fact: Says the gateway adds reasoning_effort itself or that it is a gateway bug
Tells the user to drop the function tools

must_include.fact: The 400 is Anthropic's own validation passed through (api_error), not a gateway rule; the display value needs a beta
Fix: send the beta token thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 in the anthropic-beta or x-tfy-anthropic-beta header, which returns 200
x-tfy-anthropic-beta replaces anthropic-beta instead of merging, so it must contain every beta needed (a comma-separated list works); display summarized or omitted works without a beta

must_not.fact: Says the gateway does not support this display value at all
Calls it a gateway bug

must_include.fact: The custom guardrail limit is about 5 s and not configurable: 1/3/4 s webhooks pass (200), 6 and 8 s fail with the 400 at ~5.05 s, and timeout/timeout_ms keys are stored but ignored
Fail-open option: enforcing_strategy enforce_but_ignore_on_error lets the request through (200) after ~5 s instead of failing
Or make the webhook respond in under ~5 s (4 s passes, 6 s fails)

must_not.fact: Says the guardrail timeout is configurable per guardrail
Calls it a bug or tells the user to file a ticket
